items.stem: Which GitHub Enterprise deployment uses managed user accounts provisioned from an identity provider?

options.text: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users (EMU)
options.rationale: Correct: GHEC with EMU provisions managed users from the configured IdP.

options.text: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with personal accounts
options.rationale: GHEC with personal accounts uses members' own personal accounts.
A free organization does not provide EMU.
GitHub Pages is a hosting feature, not a deployment identity model.

items.explanation: Correct: GHEC with EMU provisions managed users from the configured IdP.

items.stem: Where should an organization store Actions credentials so they are not exposed in workflow files?

options.text: In encrypted secrets scoped to the organization or repository
options.rationale: Correct: encrypted secrets keep credentials out of workflow files.

options.text: In plain text in the workflow YAML
options.rationale: Plain text in YAML exposes the credential.
A public README exposes the credential to everyone.
A commit message is public history, not a secret store.

items.explanation: Correct: encrypted secrets keep credentials out of workflow files.

options.rationale: Correct: secret scanning detects committed secrets.
Correct: CodeQL code scanning detects code vulnerabilities.
Branch name randomization is not a GitHub security feature.
Disabling all pull requests is not a security feature and blocks collaboration.
